content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Explain why equilibrium is described as 'dynamic'
State the conditions needed for equilibrium
Describe what happens at equilibrium in terms of rates
When a reversible reaction occurs in a closed system, it reaches a state called
. At equilibrium, the reaction appears to have stopped, but at the molecular level, both forward and reverse reactions continue.
A state in a reversible reaction where:
The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
The concentrations of reactants and products remain constant
Rate of forward reaction = Rate of reverse reaction
[A], [B], [C], [D] are all constant (but NOT necessarily equal)
Forward reaction: A + B → C + D continues
Reverse reaction: C + D → A + B continues
Both occur at the same rate
For every molecule of product formed, one is converted back
Overall: no net change in concentrations
A crowded escalator with people getting on at the same rate as people getting off. The number of people on the escalator stays constant, but people are still moving.
Equilibrium can only be established if:
A system where no substances can enter or leave. Energy can still transfer (not isolated).
[DIAGRAM: Graph showing rate vs time - forward rate starts high and decreases, reverse rate starts at zero and increases, until they meet]
Initially: Only reactants present, forward rate high, reverse rate zero
As reaction proceeds: Products form, forward rate decreases (less reactants)
Reverse reaction starts: Products begin converting back to reactants
Reverse rate increases as more products form
The ratio depends on the specific reaction
Equilibrium can be reached from either direction
describes the relative amounts of reactants and products.
The same equilibrium position is reached whether you start with:
Starting with H₂ and I₂ OR starting with HI reaches the same equilibrium mixture.
Dynamic equilibrium is the state of a reversible reaction in a closed system where:
The rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction
The concentrations of reactants and products remain constant
Both forward and reverse reactions continue to occur
Explain why equilibrium is described as 'dynamic' rather than 'static'.
At equilibrium, the reaction has not stopped
Both forward and reverse reactions continue to occur
Reactant particles are still forming products
Product particles are still reforming reactants
These happen at equal rates, so there is no net change
'Static' would imply nothing is happening, which is incorrect

A reversible reaction reaches equilibrium. At this point, the concentration of reactant A is 0.4 M and product C is 0.6 M. Are these concentrations equal? What happens to these concentrations over time?
The concentrations are NOT equal (0.4 M vs 0.6 M)
At equilibrium, concentrations don't have to be equal
These concentrations will remain constant over time
They are constant because rates of forward and reverse reactions are equal
For every bit of A that reacts, the same amount is reformed from C
Explain why equilibrium cannot be reached in an open container.
In an open container, substances can escape
For a reaction producing gas, the gas escapes
The reverse reaction cannot occur (products are gone)
The concentration of products cannot build up
Equal rates of forward and reverse cannot be achieved
The reaction goes to completion instead
Thinking equilibrium means the reaction has stopped
Both reactions continue at equal rates
Thinking concentrations must be equal at equilibrium
Concentrations are constant, not necessarily equal
Thinking equilibrium can only be reached from one direction
Same equilibrium is reached from any starting point
State three conditions necessary for equilibrium to be established. (3 marks)
Explain why equilibrium is described as 'dynamic'. (3 marks)
At equilibrium in the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, the concentration of nitrogen is 0.5 M, hydrogen is 1.5 M, and ammonia is 0.8 M.
a) Are these concentrations equal? (1 mark)
b) Will these concentrations change over time? Explain. (2 marks)
Sketch a graph showing how the rates of forward and reverse reactions change over time when equilibrium is reached, starting with only reactants. (3 marks)
Explain why opening a container will prevent equilibrium from being maintained. (3 marks)
When forward and reverse reaction rates are equal and concentrations are constant
A system where no matter can enter or leave
The relative amounts of reactants and products at equilibrium
Rate of forward = rate of reverse reaction
reversible reaction, closed system, constant temperature
Can be reached from any starting mixture
describes whether products or reactants are favoured
Equilibrium to the right = more products
Equilibrium to the left = more reactants
